E1.evidence: PR #56 (v4hn, 2014-03-10) names the concrete defect and its location: "The current interface returns (bool, errorstr). This is nice to have, but it's unintuitive and provokes the mistake \"not buffer.can_transform(..)\" which should really be \"not buffer.can_transform(..)[0]\". Such a bug ( as currently in tf2_ros/buffer.py:72 ) is much worse than receiving an error string without raising an exception." (https://github.com/ros/geometry2/pull/56). Maintainer confirmation: tfoote merged the consumer-side fix PR #58 ("Thanks", https://github.com/ros/geometry2/pull/58#issuecomment-37230310) as commit cec62083 "Fix the can_transform design flaw at the other end." At the PR base revision 48cc8a19 the flagged line is exactly tf2_ros/src/tf2_ros/buffer.py:72: "not self.can_transform_core(target_frame, source_frame, time) and". No reproducer or log; concrete code-level report plus maintainer-merged fix.

E2.evidence: Two separately released catkin packages in ros/geometry2: tf2_py (Python extension module tf2_py.cpp, version 0.4.10 at 48cc8a19) provides BufferCore.can_transform_core / can_transform_full_core, which at that revision return a 2-tuple: "return Py_BuildValue(\"bs\", can_transform, error_msg.c_str());" (tf2_py/src/tf2_py.cpp lines 207 and 229). tf2_ros (version 0.4.10, package.xml declares <build_depend>tf2_py</build_depend> and <run_depend>tf2_py</run_depend>) consumes them in tf2_ros/src/tf2_ros/buffer.py: "import tf2_py as tf2" and "class Buffer(tf2.BufferCore, tf2_ros.BufferInterface)", using the return value in a boolean position at lines 72 and 82. Step 2: the failure is a value crossing the library-API boundary (the provider's tuple interpreted as a bool by the consumer), so it is an interface failure even though the resolving edit is inside tf2_ros. Steps 3-5 do not apply (no deployment wiring, build, or firmware change). Interface kind: library API (Python method return value).

E3.evidence: PAIR: the output of tf2_py.BufferCore.can_transform_core (a (bool, str) tuple) feeds the loop condition of tf2_ros.Buffer.can_transform in the same process. Both units are at the same repository snapshot (48cc8a19, both 0.4.10), so no UPGRADE; no concurrency or switching is involved.

E4.evidence:
Code-level statement of the mismatch by the reporter (PR #56 body, quoted under E1) and by the fixer in the merged commit 4c496f5b message: "make can_transform actually do something

Up to now these functions never waited for a transform.
The sleep loop's condition was broken and the sleep code itself
as well." (https://github.com/ros/geometry2/commit/4c496f5b032bf0f99844e709d6405aacf3b83859). No run-time observation of the effect appears in the source, so outcome class is undocumented.

loudness_evidence: No diagnostic from any tooling appears in the source and no run of the composition is reported; the reporter characterises the defect as one that does not raise: "Such a bug ( as currently in tf2_ros/buffer.py:72 ) is much worse than receiving an error string without raising an exception." Python performs no type check on the tuple used in a boolean position, so nothing at build, import, or run would flag it; the loudness is nevertheless recorded as unknown because the source shows no observed run.

resolution.summary: Consumer-side change in tf2_ros/src/tf2_ros/buffer.py (PR #58, commit 4c496f5b, merged as cec62083): index the provider's tuple in both wait-loop conditions, "not self.can_transform_core(target_frame, source_frame, time)[0] and" and "not self.can_transform_full_core(...)[0] and"; the provider tf2_py is left unchanged. The same commit also replaces the never-reached sleep call "rospy.Duration(0.05).sleep()" with a rospy.Rate(20) object and "r.sleep()".
resolution.evidence: Accepted and merged by the maintainer (tfoote: "Thanks", https://github.com/ros/geometry2/pull/58#issuecomment-37230310; merge commit https://github.com/ros/geometry2/commit/cec62083fa3e54cf210ce8b5ea87b4c0ed60f64b), but the source shows no run of the resolved composition, so the status is recommended rather than observed.

notes: Mechanism at 48cc8a19: tf2_py's can_transform_core returns Py_BuildValue("bs", can_transform, error_msg.c_str()), a 2-tuple that is always truthy in Python, so tf2_ros's loop condition "not self.can_transform_core(...)" is always False and the timeout loop never executes; the dataset description's phrase "always yields False" refers to the negated condition (the tuple itself casts to True). The reporter first proposed changing the provider (PR #56: tf2_py returning PyBool_FromLong(...) from both bindings); the maintainer rejected it as an API change to a released package ("Can't change a released packages API.", https://github.com/ros/geometry2/pull/56#issuecomment-37214424), and the consumer was fixed instead (PR #58 "As it's important to keep the API stable, let's fix the only other end (mis)using the can_transform API in the standard ROS distribution."). PR #58 also fixes a second defect it describes as "another bug which was never discovered due to the broken can_transform check": the sleep statement rospy.Duration(0.05).sleep() inside the loop (a call into rospy, a different composition), replaced by rospy.Rate(20).sleep(); it is not a condition of this case. Both units live in the same repository and are released together (both 0.4.10), but are distinct catkin packages (tf2_py is a compiled Python extension; tf2_ros is pure Python here) that tf2_ros declares as build and run dependencies. The public wrapper Buffer.can_transform still returns the provider's tuple after the fix, so callers of tf2_ros that test that return value as a bool would have the same class of defect; the source does not document any.
